• Article 124 – Establishment of Supreme Court

• Article 131 – Original jurisdiction
• Article 137 – Review power
• Article 143 – Advisory jurisdiction

items: Questions often confuse Article 131 (Original Jurisdiction) with Article 143 (Advisory Jurisdiction).
Article 137 is frequently cited in exams regarding the Supreme Court's authority to review its prior decisions.
Article 129 is crucial for questions related to the Supreme Court's status as a 'Court of Record' and its power to punish for contempt.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 124 mandates the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court.
Article 129 declares the Supreme Court to be a Court of Record.
Article 131 specifies the Original Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in federal disputes.
Article 137 details the review power of the Supreme Court over its own judgments.
Article 143 confers Advisory Jurisdiction on the Supreme Court to advise the President.
